text:
ella-support: urgent — oncall customer (acme-inc) reporting p99 latency spike to 9s for Dedicated pool A1 during demo window. Customer also saw a couple 502s and some auth retries. They filed a ticket: https://redwood.support/ticket/ACME-789. Please triage :rotating_light:

sam-oncall: on it. Which pool exactly? Dedicated A1 or fallback? Any recent deploys?

ella-support: Dedicated pool A1 (eu-west). No deploys flagged in the last hour per deploy-bot, but we did have a capacity event around 14:02 UTC. Customer says spike started ~14:05 and lasted ~12m.

deploy-bot: no model/container deploys in last 60m for A1. Autoscaler triggered scale-up at 14:01:56 UTC. New nodes attached starting 14:03:40 UTC. Warmup logs show long GPU init (NVIDIA driver + cudnn) around 14:04:10.

marta-sre: can you paste the p95/p99 dashboards (short window) and the attach metrics (queue length, attach latency)? Also get the pool's minPool and maxPool config.

kevin-eng: grabbing metrics — p95 stayed ~600ms, p99 jumped to 9.2s between 14:05-14:17. Attach queue length spiked from 3 -> 48. Attach latency median ~1.2s but p99 for attach was 7.8s. Pool config: minPool=2, minWarm=1, maxPool=40, prewarm=false, fastAttach=false.

marta-sre: sounds like a gang-scaling cascade: many concurrent attach requests queued which then triggered node provisioning + cold GPU init causing high p99. Also saw auth retries in logs (customer service token refresh) which made requests retry and requeue.

ella-support: customer mentions billing window burst — they sent batch of test requests at 14:04.

sam-oncall: ok actionable plan: 1) enable temporary hot fallback (route to hosted variant) for this customer, 2) bump minPool to 6 for A1 for next 30m, 3) enable fastAttach prewarm for high-priority customers, 4) investigate long GPU init cause. Who can run fallback?

kevin-eng: I can flip route to hosted for ACME via console. Will do now and monitor.

kevin-eng: done — ACME traffic now routed to hosted fallback model variant. Observability: p99 for ACME dropped to 420ms within 45s. Customer confirmed immediate improvement: customer-jdoe: saw it drop to ~450ms. Thanks! :white_check_mark:

marta-sre: I'll run a quick repro locally to validate cold GPU init slowness. Posting relevant logs:

marta-sre: ```
14:03:40 kubelet: created pod redwood-infer-xxx
14:04:02 containerd: image pulled (1.2GB)
14:04:09 nvidia-init: driver probe started
14:04:15 nvidia-init: cudnn load time 6.4s
14:04:25 runtime: model init kv-cache 8s
14:04:40 attach: GPU ready
```

marta-sre: two things stand out: image pull + driver/ cudnn init ~10s total, and model warmup + KV cache population another ~8s. That matches the attach p99. We should improve prewarm and image caching strategy.

sam-oncall: immediate mitigations applied: increased minPool to 6 (A1) at 14:20 UTC, enabled image pull cache regionally, and added customer to fallback routing. I also raised customer quota temporarily to avoid auth retry storms.

ops-bot: minPool update applied: A1.minPool=6 at 14:20:32 UTC by sam-oncall. Image cache policy toggled to "regional-cache" for A1 at 14:21:10 UTC.

kevin-eng: re: root cause followup: looks like a confluence — customer burst during billing window + auth token refresh loops (their SDK retried on transient 429/401) caused request fan-out. Our autoscaler reacts but node bootstrap + model warmup created long tail.

marta-sre: proposed follow-ups (post-incident):
- enable prewarm for dedicated pools that serve priority customers
- add a fastAttach feature flag to reduce image+driver init (keep an ephemeral warm pool)
- improve image caching TTL and keep smallest runtime image for faster pulls
- add client-side guidance: exponential backoff for auth, jitter, and retry budget

sam-oncall: recording action items and owners:
- kevin: run a small canary to validate hosted fallback automation for 2 customers (48h)
- marta: prototype fastAttach prewarm and measure cold-init p99 improvement (1 week)
- infra: change pool defaults to minPool>=3 for dedicated pools that opt-in (ops ticket)

ella-support: customer happy for now, asked for postmortem and assurance this won't recur during their next billing demo (in 3 days). I've told them we'll follow up with timeline and mitigation plan.

customer-jdoe: appreciate the quick fix. Please confirm when prewarm is available.

marta-sre: will include prewarm timeline in postmortem. Thanks everyone.

sam-oncall: closing the live escalation. Marking this thread for postmortem and follow-up. :lock:

ela-support (edited): Thread resolved for now — please move to incidents if we write a postmortem.
